solution:
By the vector triple product, \(\vec{d} = (\vec{a}\times\vec{b})\times\vec{c} = (\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c})\vec{b} - (\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c})\vec{a}\).

Statement I: \(\vec{d}\) is a combination of \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\), so it is coplanar with them. True.

Statement II: \(\vec{d}\cdot\vec{c} = (\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c})(\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}) - (\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c})(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}) = 0\). (This also follows because \(\vec{d}\) is a cross product with \(\vec{c}\).) True.

Both statements are correct. Hence (C).

solution:
\(|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|^2 = 2 - 2\cos 2\theta = 4\sin^2\theta\). The condition \(|\vec{a}-\vec{b}| < 2\) gives \(4\sin^2\theta < 4\), so \(-1 < \sin\theta < 1\).

Nothing forces \(\vec{a}\neq\vec{b}\): taking \(\vec{a} = \vec{b}\) gives \(\theta = 0\) and \(\sin\theta = 0\), which is allowed. So the strict lower bound \(0 < \sin\theta\) in (A) fails. Options (B) and (C) fail too, since \(\sin\theta\) can be \(0\) and can come close to \(1\).

The one statement that always holds is \(-1 < \sin\theta < 1\). Hence (D).

solution:
Three vectors are coplanar when their scalar triple product is zero:

\(\begin{vmatrix} 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & m & n \end{vmatrix} = 1(3n-2m) + 1(2n-2) + 1(2m-3) = 5n - 5 = 0\), so \(n = 1\).

Then \(|\vec{c}|^2 = 1 + m^2 + 1 = 6\) gives \(m^2 = 4\), so \(m = \pm 2\).

So \(m = \pm 2\) and \(n = 1\). Hence (D).

solution:
Statement 1: \(\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}+\overrightarrow{CA} = \vec{0}\) by the triangle law. Correct.

Statement 2: \(\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC} = \overrightarrow{AC} = -\overrightarrow{CA}\), so the expression is \(-2\overrightarrow{CA} \neq \vec{0}\). Incorrect.

Statement 3: \(\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{CA} = \overrightarrow{CB}\), so the expression is \(\overrightarrow{CB}-\overrightarrow{BC} = 2\overrightarrow{CB} \neq \vec{0}\). Incorrect.

Statement 4: \(\overrightarrow{BA}-\overrightarrow{BC} = \overrightarrow{CA}\), so the expression is \(2\overrightarrow{CA} \neq \vec{0}\). Incorrect.

Exactly one statement is correct. Hence (A).

solution:
\(|\vec{a}+\vec{b}| = 1\) gives \(1 + 1 + 2\,\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = 1\), so \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\). In the same way \(|\vec{b}+\vec{c}| = 1\) gives \(\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\).

\(|\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}| = 1\) gives \(3 + 2(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}+\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}+\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}) = 1\), so the sum of the three dot products is \(-1\). Hence \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c} = -1 + \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} = 0\).

So the angle between \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{c}\) is \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\). Hence (C).
